grammar_concept.title: Second Conditional: if + Past Simple, would + base verb
grammar_concept.rule: Use the Second Conditional for imaginary or unlikely situations in the present or future, and their imagined result: "if" + Past Simple, "would" + base verb.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Ao contrário do First Conditional (situações reais e possíveis), o Second Conditional é para situações imaginárias, hipotéticas, pouco prováveis ou impossíveis.
grammar_concept.example: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world. If I were you, I would talk to her.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Se ganhasse a lotaria, viajaria pelo mundo. Se eu fosse tu, falava com ela.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Depois de aprender o First Conditional, é comum tentar aplicar a mesma estrutura aqui e usar "will" na parte do "if", ou usar o Present Simple em vez do Past Simple ("If I win the lottery" em vez de "If I won the lottery") — porque o português usa o pretérito imperfeito do conjuntivo ("se ganhasse"), que não parece obviamente "passado" a um aluno. Também é comum esquecer que, no Second Conditional formal, usa-se "were" para todas as pessoas ("If I were", não "If I was").
grammar_concept.correction: A parte com "if" usa sempre Past Simple (won, had, went), nunca "will" nem Present Simple. O resultado usa "would" + verbo base. Com o verbo "be", a forma mais correta e formal é "were" para todas as pessoas: "If I were you...", embora "was" seja aceitável em contextos informais.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: A dar um conselho: "If I were you, I would ask for a pay rise."

vocabulary.definition_en: not real; existing only in the mind
example_sentences: Second Conditional sentences describe imaginary situations.
It's unlikely to rain today, but take an umbrella just in case.

vocabulary.definition_en: a game in which people buy tickets with numbers, and prizes are given to randomly chosen numbers
example_sentences: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.

exercises.prompt: Complete: If I ___ (win) the lottery, I would travel the world.
exercises.explanation: A parte com "if" usa Past Simple ("won"), não Present Simple nem "will".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "win" (Present Simple) aqui é um erro comum, misturando com a estrutura do First Conditional.

correct_answer: If I were you, I would talk to her.
distractors: If I was you, I would talked to her.
If I am you, I would talk to her.
If I were you, I will talk to her.
exercises.explanation: Forma tradicionalmente correta do Second Conditional com "be": "If I were you".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "was" em vez de "were" é aceitável informalmente, mas "were" é a forma mais segura e mais ensinada.

exercises.explanation: "Unlikely" é o oposto de "likely" — algo pouco provável de acontecer.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What would the speaker do with more free time?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "If I had more free time, I would learn a new language."
exercises.transcript: If I had more free time, I would learn a new language. It's unlikely to happen this year, though, with my work schedule.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "If she had a bigger budget, she would hire more staff. It's an imaginary scenario for now, since the company can't afford it this year." What would she do with a bigger budget?
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "she would hire more staff".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Se eu fosse tu, aceitava o emprego."
correct_answer: If I were you, I would accept the job.
If I were you, I'd accept the job.
exercises.explanation: "If I were you" + would é a estrutura correta do Second Conditional.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "will" em vez de "would" no resultado é um erro comum, misturando com o First Conditional.

steps.content: "Would" almost always contracts to 'd in speech: "I would" → "I'd" /aɪd/. In the if-clause, "were" is often given slightly more stress to signal the hypothetical, unreal nature of the sentence.

steps.prompt: Talk about 3 imaginary situations and what you would do — winning the lottery, having a super power, living somewhere else.
Write 5 sentences about imaginary or unlikely situations using the Second Conditional.
